papers.title: Global well-posedness and long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu--Eckhaus equation
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness in the Schwartz space and establish long-time asymptotics for the focusing coupled Kundu--Eckhaus (CKE) equation. For data with no discrete spectrum or real-axis spectral singularities, we analyze the associated matrix Riemann--Hilbert problem by the Deift--Zhou nonlinear steepest descent method. A quantitative local expansion of the full matrix factor near the stationary point identifies the unitary factor in the leading vector term. We combine an estimate for the full matrix coefficient at infinity with exact mass identities. This gives joint error estimates for the gauge-equivalent coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger solution, the cumulative mass, and the gauge phase. These joint estimates yield an explicit asymptotic formula for CKE radiation with an $O(t^{-1}\log t)$ remainder, uniformly for $x/t$ in compact subsets of $\mathbb R$. We also compute the reflection coefficient and the unitary endpoint factor to visualize the asymptotic solution.

papers.title: A local Yang-Baxter obstruction for the hard-square model
papers.abstract: Many exact solutions of two-dimensional lattice models rest on an analytic family of weights satisfying the Yang-Baxter equation. The hard-hexagon model was solved in this way, while the neighbouring hard-square model has no known closed form. We determine the height alphabets that encode hard squares without hidden heights, and there are exactly two connected ones, the occupation variables themselves and the four heights of Andrews, Baxter and Forrester. Hard hexagons is integrable on both, but no analytic Yang-Baxter family of face weights passes through hard squares at nonzero activity on either. The difference lies in the exclusion rule, which for hard squares turns a few Yang-Baxter equations into polynomial identities that force auxiliary weights to vanish. A closed form for hard squares is not excluded, but a solution by this route would have to leave these encodings or go beyond a single analytic family through the model. Encodings with hidden heights remain open.

papers.title: Comments on flavor symmetry breaking and three-dimensional superconformal index
papers.abstract: We investigate the superconformal index of a three-dimensional $SU(2)$ ${\mathcal N}=2$ supersymmetric QCD with $N_f=4$ flavors. This theory confines with the breaking of a global symmetry. We obtain the index of this theory by integrating out a flavor from the theory with $N_f=6$ flavors. The superconformal index of the theory vanishes for generic values of the flavor fugacities. However, the specific choice of fugacities allows us to describe the flavor symmetry-breaking phenomenon.

papers.title: On integrals of non-autonomous dynamical systems in finite characteristic
papers.abstract: We use a difference Lax form to construct simultaneous integrals of motion of the fourth Painlev\'e equation and the difference second Painlev\'e equation over fields with finite characteristic $p>0$. For $p\neq 3$, we show that the integrals can be normalised to be completely invariant under the corresponding extended affine Weyl group action. We show that components of reducible fibres of integrals correspond to reductions to Riccatti equations. We further describe a method to construct non-rational algebraic solutions in a given positive characteristic. We also discuss a projective reduction of the integrals.

papers.title: The \texorpdfstring{$\mathbf N$-soliton}{N-soliton} solution formula for the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation
papers.abstract: An explicit formula is presented for the $\mathbf N$-soliton solution to the Kaup--Kupershmidt equation, for any positive integer $\mathbf N,$ by using the input data set consisting of $\mathbf N$ distinct positive $p_j$-values and $\mathbf N$ arbitrarily chosen positive $c_j$-values. The formula is derived from the solution to the inverse scattering problem for a third-order linear operator in the reflectionless case with the $p_j$-values related to the bound-state poles of a transmission coefficient and the $c_j$-values related to the bound-state dependency constants. It is indicated how the formula is constructed from the solution to a Riemann--Hilbert problem and from the solution to a Marchenko integral equation used in the formulation of the aforementioned inverse scattering problem.

papers.title: On equivalence between solution structures of the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations
papers.abstract: We establish an exact correspondence between the quasi-Wronskian and quasi-Grammian constructions for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills (ASDYM) equations with complex \(2\times2\) matrix-valued fields. Starting from vacuum wave functions associated with \(2M\) pairwise distinct nonzero constant spectral parameters, we restrict attention to a nonempty local domain on which the corresponding interpolation matrix is invertible. We show that both constructions are governed by the same uniquely solvable matrix-polynomial interpolation problem. In particular, the quasi-Wronskian Darboux polynomial \(T(\lambda)\) and the quasi-Grammian rational dressing matrix \(W(\lambda)\) satisfy \[ T(\lambda)=q_\xi(\lambda)W(\lambda), \] where \(q_\xi(\lambda)\) is the monic scalar polynomial whose zeros are the prescribed poles of \(W(\lambda)\). This identity yields explicit relations between the corresponding Yang and potential matrices and shows that the two constructions generate identical ASDYM gauge potentials in the same gauge.
